newsitem.title: UK: Colombia oil pipeline ready, will open next month.
newsitem.headline: Colombia oil pipeline ready, will open next month.

text.p: A new $2 billion pipeline which could increase Colombia's oil output by 140,000 barrels per day (bpd) by the end of the year has already been completed and may be open by the middle of July, a senior oil official said.
"It is already completed... and it will enter operation by mid July," Colombia's Energy and Mines minister Rodrigo Villamizar told reporters.

Current production from the Cusiana and Cupiagua fields are expected to rise to around 320,000 barrels per day after the new pipeline to Covenas to the Atlantic is opened and Villamizar said he expected 550,000 barrels per day by the end of the year.

Total Colombian oil output will be 750,000 barrels per day by then, added Villamizar, who was in London to discuss current oil contracts with British companies and to promote some of his country's energy assets which are soon to be privatised.

But the export surge from Cusiana and Cupiagua may not be felt until August, as some time will initially be spent filling lines and tanks along the new OCENSA pipe system - which is an addition to smaller existing pipeline capacity.
Analysts expect the increased exports of the sought-after oil to conflict head-on with North Sea and West African supplies in the Atlantic baisin.

British Petroleum Co Plc operates the Cusiana and Cupiagua fields with a 19 percent interest. Other partners are Total Petroleum, with 19 percent, and Triton Energy with 12 percent. State oil company Ecopetrol holds 50 percent.

Villamizar also said his country needs to sign more lenient oil contracts to stop oil production declining towards the end of the century, but added that the government needs to overcome strong political obstacles to do so, a senior oil official said.
"We are fully aware that we have one of the largest state takes in the world - between 81 and 83 percent of the money generated goes to the government."
"We are going to have to reduce the state take but it is a very, very touchy issue in Colombia. Every man in the street wants to give his opinion about this."
He said that about 40 wildcats were drilled in Colombia last year - compared to some 12,000 in Canada.

"We need to increase exploration activity. There is a lot of potential but we need a lot of investment. It is a very costly operation because of the geology," he said, adding that the costs of drilling one well were as much as ten times the world average.
But he gave no more details about, or any timetable for, the creation of new oil contracts.
